summary:
ANCASH DEPARTMENT STANDS UNDER PERU'S NATIONAL FRAMEWORK. The source inventory contains no departmental ordinance, municipal decree or incident series specific to Ancash; every available item is national in scope, and the national framework set out here is what a visitor to Ancash is scored against.

Peru does not criminalise trans identity, but the national Congress has legislated against trans people's use of public facilities, hate-crime protection for LGBT people has been removed from the Penal Code, and recorded violence against trans women is rising.

In February 2025 the congressional Comision de Mujer y Familia approved by unanimity a dictamen merging bills 6506 and 8457, sponsored by Jorge Montoya and Alejandro Munante, prohibiting any person from entering public sanitary facilities designated for the sex opposite to their birth sex. The exceptions are narrow, covering custody situations and cases where required, including accompanying minors, elderly people or people with disabilities, and the text would oblige venues not to post ambiguous restroom signs. The measure still required plenary backing. The reported trigger was a July 2023 complaint over gendered restroom labels at Lima's Jorge Chavez international airport. Activist Gianna Camacho argued the measure is discriminatory and that enforcement would rest on security staff checking the DNI to decide whether a woman entering a women's restroom is trans or cisgender.

On Wednesday 2 April 2025 the plenary of Congress approved the dictamen of the Ley que fortalece el derecho a la indemnidad sexual de los ninos y adolescentes and waived a second vote. Its Article 5.1 prohibits persons from entering or using public sanitary facilities designated for a sex other than their birth sex. The human-rights institute IDEHPUCP of the Pontifical Catholic University of Peru reads Article 5 as a direct breach of equality and non-discrimination under Article 2(2) of the Peruvian Constitution and Article 1.1 of the American Convention on Human Rights, resting on the stereotype that trans people are more prone to enter restrooms to harass or sexually abuse minors.

IDEHPUCP also records SPC-INDECOPI Resolution 0735-2022, which dismissed a trans woman's discrimination complaint against the gym chain SmartFit after the company grounded bathroom assignment on the sex recorded in the DNI, and states that gender-identity recognition in Peru remains long, costly and invasive.

Violence against trans people is documented and under-recorded. The Observatorio de Derechos TLGBI of Universidad Peruana Cayetano Heredia recorded 54 killings of LGBTI people and 170 rights-violation cases between 2020 and 2023; the homicide victims were 30 trans women, 23 gay men and one lesbian. Nineteen killings occurred in 2023 alone, 12 of them trans women, and the killers were not identified in 26 of the 54 homicides, including 13 of the 19 in 2023.

Among the 2023 cases, trans sex worker Rubi Torres Silvano, 31, was kidnapped from central Lima in February 2023 by a 'Los Gallegos' extortion gang and killed in Carabayllo with some 30 gunshots; Priscila Aguado Huatuco, 30, had been shot days earlier. Two killers were arrested in March 2023. The state has not incorporated sexual orientation or gender identity into its crime-registration systems, so hate crimes cannot be prosecuted as such.
tangentialFactors:
The Inter-American Court of Human Rights held in Advisory Opinion OC-24/17 that gender identity falls under protected personal autonomy and that states must guarantee trans people's full rights, a standard the bathroom provisions sit against.

Peru's Congress voted in 2017 to strip LGBT protections from the new Penal Code's hate-crime provisions, with Popular Force and Alliance for Progress members carrying the repeal after an April Constitutional Committee vote and amid a petition claiming one million signatures. The outcome left Peru one of only three South American countries, with Paraguay and Guyana, lacking LGBT anti-discrimination coverage in hate-crime law.

In December 2025 three police officers, Dino Ponce, Luis Quispe and Juan León, were sentenced to 17 years' imprisonment for the rape and torture of Azul Rojas Marín, a trans woman and LGBTI activist, nearly 20 years after the attack and after years of litigation. It was Peru's first conviction in a case motivated by sexual discrimination and, per BBC News Mundo, the Inter-American Court of Human Rights' first torture-by-discrimination case in the region's history; the case reached the Court through the Inter-American Commission on Human Rights.

A 2024 report found hate crimes rising in Peru with trans women most affected, and its co-author Gianna Camacho, a trans journalist and human-rights defender, stressed that the recorded figures are only a sub-registry.

Enforcement of the bathroom restriction reaches private and public life. A consumer-protection body dismissed a trans woman's discrimination complaint against a gym that enforced the policy. On television, presenter Ana María Salcedo of Willax TV publicly harassed Susel Paredes, the first openly lesbian member of Congress, telling her to 'go use the men's room'.

Two protective developments are on record. In June 2024 Peru's health authorities removed outdated pathologising terminology for gender diversity from official health guidance, described as a step toward dignity for trans patients in healthcare settings. In July 2025 a Lima constitutional court, after an activist legal challenge, ruled an anti-equality decree unconstitutional.

Speech and association are constrained by the same legislative package. Vague child-protection articles in the April 2025 law, including an article 4 ban on media and advertising content, enable censorship of identity, artistic and educational material, and the minimum sentence for obscenity was raised from three to four years; Human Rights Watch states that child protection is a pretext for repression and the scapegoating of trans people.
localsOnly:
The sex recorded in the DNI is the operative marker in practice: venues assign restrooms on it, and a national consumer-protection body has upheld that approach against a discrimination complaint. A trans resident's document marker, not their presentation, is what staff are being told to read.

Gender-identity recognition in Peru remains long, costly and invasive, so a resident's identity documents may continue to contradict their lived gender for years.

Because sexual orientation and gender identity are absent from the state's crime-registration systems, a resident who reports an attack cannot have the hate motivation recorded or prosecuted as such; the 54 killings recorded between 2020 and 2023 and the unidentified killers in 26 of those cases reflect that gap.

Residents retain a litigation route: an activist challenge before a Lima constitutional court succeeded in July 2025 in striking an anti-equality decree, and the Azul Rojas Marín case produced Peru's first conviction for discrimination-motivated torture in December 2025.

Health guidance no longer uses pathologising terminology for gender diversity following the June 2024 change, which affects how trans patients are treated in clinical settings. Inclusive signage such as 'women in their diversity' is banned under the April 2025 package.
outOfScopeNotes:
No Ancash-specific source appears in the inventory. Whether the April 2025 restroom provision has been enforced in Ancash venues, and whether any complaint, police report or court filing arising from it has been brought in the department, is unresolved and not sourced here.

The national killing and violation figures for 2020-2023 are not broken down by department, so Ancash's share of the recorded violence is unresolved.

The February 2025 dictamen of bills 6506 and 8457 is reported as approved by committee and still awaiting plenary backing; whether those bills were enacted separately from the April 2025 law, or folded into it, is not sourced.

Whether security staff at Ancash public facilities actually check the DNI to determine restroom access, as Gianna Camacho warned would occur nationally, is not documented for this department.
